query: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but very poor room-temperature ductility, while its irradiation resistance has primarily been proposed by first-principles calculations. What intervention could improve its room-temperature ductility without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the untreated NbMoTaW baseline under room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation assessments, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Adding ~0.5 at% boron to equiatomic NbMoTaW will improve its room-temperature ductility by promoting boron segregation to grain boundaries and increasing their cohesive energy, without significantly degrading its 1600 °C yield strength or irradiation resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic NbMoTaW single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy, as-cast, grain size ~50 µm, room-temperature tensile ductility <5%, yield strength ~600 MPa at 1600 °C, irradiation swelling <1% at 10 dpa.
generation.intervention: Incorporate 0.5 at% B via powder metallurgy blending, homogenize at 1500 °C/24 h, then hot-isostatic-pressing to full density.
generation.conditions: Single-phase BCC retained, grain size 10–100 µm, B content 0.1–1 at%, tensile tests at room temperature and 1600 °C, irradiation to 10 dpa at 300 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Segregation of boron atoms to grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: Boron lowers grain-boundary energy and increases cohesive strength, reducing propensity for intergranular fracture at room temperature, while remaining in solid solution or at boundaries so as not to form embrittling precipitates or defect sinks that would impair high-temperature strength or irradiation tolerance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Room-temperature tensile elongation increases by 2–3× relative to baseline; yield strength at 1600 °C decreases by <5%; irradiation swelling and creep rate remain within ±10% of baseline.
generation.baseline: As-cast NbMoTaW: <5% room-temperature elongation, ~600 MPa yield strength at 1600 °C, <1% swelling at 10 dpa.
generation.boundary: Valid for B contents of 0.1–1 at%, grain sizes 10–100 µm, single-phase BCC; irradiation temperatures ≤500 °C.
generation.uncertainty: High-temperature and irradiation performance projections are extrapolated from limited boron-doping data in simpler BCC refractory alloys; effect magnitudes are approximate.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two NbMoTaW samples: control and 0.5 at% B doped, identical processing. Use TEM-EDS and atom-probe tomography to quantify B segregation. Perform uniaxial tensile tests at 25 °C and 1600 °C. Irradiate both samples to 10 dpa at 300 °C and measure swelling.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis falsified if B-doped alloy shows <10% improvement in room-temperature elongation, >10% drop in 1600 °C yield strength, >10% increase in swelling, or lack of measurable B segregation at grain boundaries.
